questions.prompt: What does a MAC (Message Authentication Code) provide using only symmetric cryptography?
questions.explanation: A MAC combines a hash function with a shared secret key to prove integrity and authenticity.

questions.prompt: What problem does Diffie-Hellman / ECDH solve?
options: Establishing a shared secret key over an insecure channel without transmitting it directly
questions.explanation: Diffie-Hellman/ECDH lets two parties derive a shared secret without ever transmitting the secret itself.

questions.prompt: What does 'non-repudiation' mean in the context of digital signatures?
options: The signer can later deny signing
The signer cannot credibly deny having signed the message
The message can be edited after signing
questions.explanation: Non-repudiation means the signer can't credibly deny they signed the message, since only their private key could have produced it.

questions.prompt: What TLS handshake step establishes the shared symmetric session key?
questions.explanation: The key exchange step (commonly ECDHE) is what allows client and server to derive a shared symmetric key.

questions.prompt: Why does poor key management matter even with a strong algorithm?
options: It doesn't matter if the algorithm is strong
Weak randomness or poor storage/rotation can undermine security regardless of algorithm strength
Keys never need to be rotated
questions.explanation: A strong algorithm can still be undermined by weak randomness, poor storage, or lack of key rotation — key management is a common real-world failure point.

questions.prompt: Which design approach follows Kerckhoffs' principle?
options: Keep the algorithm secret so attackers cannot study it.
Assume attackers know the algorithm and rely only on the secrecy of the key.
questions.explanation: Kerckhoffs' principle asks that a system stay secure even when everything except the key is public.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: A ciphertext encrypted in ECB mode contains two identical blocks. What does an observer learn?
options: The two plaintext blocks were identical.
The key was reused with the same nonce.
Nothing, because the match is random.
questions.explanation: ECB is deterministic under one key, so equal ciphertext blocks come from equal plaintext blocks.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: What does AES-GCM provide that AES-CTR alone does not?
options: Detection of modified ciphertext or associated data.
questions.explanation: GCM adds an authentication tag over the ciphertext and the associated data; decryption fails if either is altered.

source.title: A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography

questions.prompt: Why does an attacker who can find two messages with the same hash threaten digital signatures?
options: A signature on one message is also valid for the other, so the signed message can be swapped.
questions.explanation: Signatures are made over the digest. If two messages share a digest, one signature covers both.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: Why is h(key || message) with SHA-256 a poor MAC?
options: Length extension lets an attacker forge a tag for a longer message.
SHA-256 outputs are not fixed length.
questions.explanation: SHA-2 hashes blocks sequentially, so a known digest can be extended with more data without the key. HMAC avoids this.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: What does a random per-user salt protect against when storing password hashes?
options: Precomputed tables, and identical passwords producing identical hashes.
questions.explanation: A unique salt forces an attacker to attack each hash separately and makes rainbow tables useless.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: What does multiplying a schoolbook RSA ciphertext by 2^e mod n do to the decrypted plaintext?
questions.explanation: RSA is malleable: (2^e · m^e)^d = 2m mod n. Padding such as OAEP prevents this.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: What defeats a man-in-the-middle attack on Diffie-Hellman?
options: Authenticating the public values, for example with certificates and signatures.
Encrypting the public values with AES.
questions.explanation: The attack works whenever public keys are not authenticated; certificates bind keys to identities.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: In a hash-then-sign scheme such as ECDSA, which key signs and what is signed?
options: The private key signs a hash of the message.
The public key signs the message.
A shared key signs the hash.
questions.explanation: Only the private key can produce a valid signature; the digest is signed so long messages are handled efficiently.

source.title: Understanding Cryptography: From Established Symmetric and Asymmetric Ciphers to Post-Quantum Algorithms
source.authors: Christof Paar, Jan Pelzl, Tim Güneysu

questions.prompt: Which parts of a TLS 1.3 connection are directly threatened by Shor's algorithm?
options: The key exchange and the signatures in certificates.
questions.explanation: Shor's algorithm breaks factoring and discrete logarithms, the basis of Diffie-Hellman and RSA or ECDSA signatures.
